hero_kpi_rationale: Organic sales growth excluding foreign exchange impact and acquisitions and disposals. This is Unilever's central KPI as it captures the real demand dynamics (price + volume) and reflects the effectiveness of its premium brand strategy and pricing power in a mature sector.

kpis.name: Organic Sales Growth
kpis.explanation: Sales growth excluding foreign exchange impacts and acquisitions or disposals.
kpis.description: Sales growth adjusted for currency effects and scope changes. A key performance indicator at Unilever.
kpis.signal: Solid organic growth despite an inflationary environment.

kpis.name: Volume Growth
kpis.explanation: Increase in quantities sold, excluding price increases.
kpis.description: Growth in physical volume sold, indicating brands are gaining market share.
kpis.signal: Volume growth: real demand is rising, not just price inflation.

kpis.name: Premium Sales Mix
kpis.explanation: Proportion of sales from premium brands.
kpis.description: Growing share of sales from premium brands, signaling successful value-up strategy.
kpis.signal: Successful premiumization: more consumers choosing premium products.

kpis.name: Share of 30 Power Brands
kpis.explanation: Sales contribution from the 30 main brands such as Dove or Knorr.
kpis.description: The 30 Power Brands represent two-thirds of sales, demonstrating the strength of flagship brands.
kpis.signal: Major brands driving growth: focused strategy delivering results.

kpis.name: Adjusted Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit margin before exceptional items.
kpis.description: Adjusted operating margin, excluding non-recurring items, reflecting underlying profitability.
kpis.signal: Stable margin despite cost pressures: strong operational management.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow
kpis.description: Strong Free Cash Flow, supporting shareholder returns and financial flexibility.
kpis.signal: Abundant cash for dividends and share buybacks.

kpis.name: Research and Development Expenses
kpis.explanation: Investment in innovation and new product development.
kpis.description: R&D focused on Power Brands and sustainability, a key differentiation driver. Unilever employs over 500 PhDs in its research organization.

kpis.name: Ice Cream Division Spin-off
kpis.explanation: Announcement of the spin-off of the Unilever Ice Cream division by 2026.
kpis.description: Unilever announced the separation of its Ice Cream division, valued at $1.8 billion, to refocus on core segments.
kpis.signal: Major demerger underway: strategic transformation to refocus on core business.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du résultat net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

risks.title: Indirect tax litigation in Brazil related to 2001 reorganization
risks.score_rationale: Identified as 'critical audit matter' by KPMG, with a tax assessment valuation amount of 3,557 Bn EUR as of 31/12/2025 and risk of additional assessments for periods not yet evaluated; very strong language ('high degree of complexity', 'high degree of judgement', 'possible material tax assessments'); persistent trend across multiple fiscal years; maximum weight in Litigation category for a listed group.

risks.title: Integration risk of recent acquisitions (Dr. Squatch, Minimalist, Wild)
risks.score_rationale: Three acquisitions completed in 2025 representing 3.0% of total assets, excluded from internal control assessment scope; audit report explicitly highlights exclusion of these entities from ICFR perimeter; 'new' trend reflecting accelerated acquisition strategy; non-negligible risk of operational integration and internal control.

risks.title: Exposure to hyperinflationary markets and emerging macroeconomic instability
risks.score_rationale: Net monetary loss of 68 M EUR in 2025 (vs 201 M EUR in 2024) linked to hyperinflationary economies (Argentina, Turkey); hyperinflation adjustment of 17 M EUR in 2025 vs 880 M EUR in 2024; structural presence in volatile emerging markets; 'down' trend in intensity but persistent structural risk for a group generating significant revenue in these zones.

risks.title: Strategic divestitures and portfolio execution risk
risks.score_rationale: Major divestiture of Ice Cream division (spin-off in 2025, disposal gain of 3,373 Bn EUR), prior disposals (Russia, Elida Beauty, Pureit, Qinyuan in 2024, Suave in 2023); goodwill reduction from 22,311 Bn EUR to 17,709 Bn EUR and tangible fixed assets from 11,669 Bn EUR to 8,992 Bn EUR; 'up' trend reflecting active portfolio transformation with execution and valuation risks.

risks.title: Competitive pressure on brands and market share erosion
risks.score_rationale: Revenue declines from 52,479 Bn EUR (2024) to 50,503 Bn EUR (2025) on continuing operations, signaling pressure on volumes and/or pricing; acquisition strategy for premium brands (Dr. Squatch, Minimalist, Wild) reveals need for repositioning against agile competitors; 'stable' to 'up' trend in a highly competitive FMCG sector.

risks.title: Risk of goodwill and brand intangible asset impairment
risks.score_rationale: Goodwill of 17,709 Bn EUR and intangible assets of 17,055 Bn EUR on 2025 balance sheet, representing over 49% of total non-current assets; significant goodwill reduction (4,602 Bn EUR) linked to disposals; any deterioration in acquired brand prospects (Dr. Squatch, Minimalist, etc.) could trigger material impairments; 'stable' trend but structurally elevated risk.

risks.title: Geopolitical risk from presence in tension-prone markets
risks.score_rationale: Disposal of Russian operations in 2024 (disposal loss included in 229 M EUR loss on divestitures); residual exposure to politically unstable emerging markets; 'stable' trend following Russian exposure reduction; group remains present in high geopolitical risk zones (Middle East, South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa).

risks.title: Environmental and regulatory risk linked to sustainability commitments
risks.score_rationale: Unilever has historically made ambitious public commitments (plastics, carbon emissions, sustainable supply chain) subject to increasing regulatory and NGO scrutiny; revision of certain sustainability targets in 2024 generated criticism; 'up' trend with tightening ESG regulations (CSRD, CSDDD in Europe); significant category weight for a mass consumer goods group.

ai_positioning.summary: The company UL does not mention artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related topics in its 10-K/20-F filing.
